title: Brown repeats the vacuum experiment at Bahnson's Institute of Field Physics
place_text: Institute of Field Physics, North Carolina

tellings.quote: And then he does the same experiment at the Bonson labs at the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina.

plain: In the 1950s, Michels says, the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown repeated his experiment with charged devices in a vacuum at the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina, a lab backed by a businessman named Agnew Bahnson. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. It matters to him because a result that held up in a vacuum would suggest the effect was not just moving air.
